clue.text: Harry, Liam, Louis, Niall and Zayn initially await G&T mid song

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or worry, so these letters are roughed up into a new order
takes the opening letter of each of the four names and the 'and' between them

parts.note: taken as written
G and T, the letters of a gin and tonic, with the ampersand dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: The members of One Direction are waiting for gin and tonics halfway through a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The five names are the boy band One Direction, but Harry's name is the anagram signal, not a source of a letter. Initials L, L, N, A, Z join AWAIT, GT and MID to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Australia's famous unofficial national ballad, about a swagman camped by a billabong.

clue.text: Wozniak's first to develop an Apple product complete with IT support widget

indicators.note: in a down clue the IT sits beneath everything else, holding it up
takes just the opening letter of the name Wozniak

parts.note: to hatch a plan is to develop it
an and a are both the indefinite article
the Mac is Apple's computer
all means the whole, complete
taken as written

explanation.surface: Steve Wozniak, Apple co-founder, sets out to build a gadget with its own tech support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is only a joining word; 'support' places IT at the foot of this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are vague placeholder words for a gadget or thing whose proper name escapes the speaker.

clue.text: The sort of song you can rock out to

definitions.text: The sort of song you can rock out to

parts.words: The sort of song you can rock out to
parts.note: sounds like a hard-rock anthem, but the rocking is of a cradle and 'out' means asleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock out' suggests loud guitars; read it as rocking a baby until it is out cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing song sung to a baby being gently rocked until it falls asleep.

clue.text: A&R man from The Happy Mondays recalled one of many bands?

indicators.note: called back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: A and R, the artists-and-repertoire department of a record label, with the ampersand dropped
Bez, the maraca-shaking dancer of the Manchester band Happy Mondays

explanation.surface: A record-label talent scout from the Happy Mondays remembers one of the many groups he dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bands' looks like music groups; here it means stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is covered in black and white stripes, so it is something with many stripes.

clue.text: Honourable, say to replace old boy before court reveals carelessness

indicators.note: puts the first part ahead of the court abbreviation
the word for 'say' takes the place of the old boy inside the first word

parts.note: noble means honourable, of high moral character
OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
say is short for 'for example', abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: An honourable old boy in court is shown up for being careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect is failure to take proper care, the same idea as carelessness as a noun.

clue.text: Don of gardening framing cover of horticultural magazine?

indicators.note: the gardener's name surrounds the letters inside it like a picture frame

parts.note: Monty Don is the BBC's best-known gardening presenter

indicators.note: a cover wraps round the outside, so take the first and last letters of horticultural

explanation.surface: Monty Don appears on the front of a gardening magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a magazine is often a periodical published once a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A periodical published every month is commonly called by that adjective used as a noun.

clue.text: Academic to mention upset after different zip's lowered almost all the way

indicators.note: puts the reversed word for mention after the first part
in a down answer the zero slides down the word to the second-last place

parts.note: other means different
zip means nothing, zero, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to mention

explanation.surface: An academic mentions being upset after a different zip on his trousers slipped down nearly all the way.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'lowered' means moved further down the light and 'upset' means read upwards; 'zip' is nothing, the zero shape of O.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic question is merely theoretical, of interest in principle but with no practical consequence.

clue.text: Miserable service begins disappointment

indicators.note: the service word comes at the start of the answer

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and is replayed
down means low in spirits, miserable

explanation.surface: Poor customer service is where the disappointment starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A letdown is an anticlimax, something that falls short of expectations.

clue.text: Ariana Grande's debut set night apart somehow as contrary to norm

indicators.note: the letters are taken apart and put back together in some new way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so take the opening letter of Grande

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The pop star Ariana Grande's first gig was set on a different night, against the usual run of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually, ARIANA itself is fodder while only Grande gives its initial G; with SETNIGHT they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from woodworking: cutting across the fibres rather than along them, so contrary to what is natural.

clue.text: Spontaneously rejecting German newspaper article

indicators.note: throwing back, so the letters are read from the other end

parts.note: Bild is Germany's best-selling tabloid daily
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone impulsively turns down an article written for a German paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak this way is to improvise, without preparation or a script.

clue.text: Red colour finishing off drink

parts.note: ginger is the colour of red hair

indicators.note: the colour word loses its finishing letter

parts.note: teal is a blue-green colour

explanation.surface: A red shade is the final touch to a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion of the root in hot water, a warming beverage.

clue.text: Revolutionary touring a radical pantomime

indicators.note: going round, so the revolutionary's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born Marxist revolutionary
rad is slang for radical, extreme

explanation.surface: Che Guevara travelling with a radical companion is a farce.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean an absurd pretence or empty show, and the game itself is mimed acting.

clue.text: Spike not good after tip removed from pointed spear

indicators.note: the second part comes after the first
the word for pointed loses its front tip, its first letter

parts.note: sharp means pointed

indicators.note: says the letter for good is to be left out

parts.note: Spike Milligan was one of the Goons of the British radio comedy The Goon Show

explanation.surface: A spike that isn't any good once the point is snapped off a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like part of the definition but leads to Spike Milligan, a Goon; take out G and add to HARP.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon is a barbed spear thrown or fired at whales or large fish.

clue.text: Irregularity of arrangement up to now — with millions invested in railway

indicators.note: put inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: as yet means up to now
M is millions, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: An irregular arrangement so far, with millions sunk into the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a lack of balance or symmetry, parts not matching each other.

clue.text: Something meant to stun soldier in field hospital with a little cut — that hurt

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: MASH is a US Mobile Army Surgical Hospital
GI is an American private soldier

indicators.note: just a little of the word cut, its first letter

parts.note: ow is the exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A soldier in an army field hospital with a small cut cries out at the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' places the soldier and the bit of cut inside MASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror's performance aims to amaze and astonish its audience.

clue.text: Remove jacket to smarten up jumper

indicators.note: strip off the outer layer, the first and last letters

parts.note: to groom is to smarten up

explanation.surface: Take off your jacket to tidy yourself and show off your sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' is the British word for a sweater, which suits the clothing surface, but here it is the kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo, in its Australian short form, is the great jumping animal.

clue.text: Belief of refugee finally making it into temporary accommodation

indicators.note: getting inside, so the letter goes within the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter

indicators.note: takes the last letter of refugee

explanation.surface: A refugee holds on to a belief as they finally reach a temporary shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or doctrine held to be true, a core conviction.

clue.text: Copying flap in GAP trousers

indicators.note: as a verb, trousers means pockets, keeps inside, so the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: A fly flap in Gap-brand trousers is a copy of another design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like clothing; it is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Aping is imitating, mimicking the way an ape is thought to.

clue.text: Singer performing in Italian club

indicators.note: the performing word sits inside the club's name

parts.note: Inter Milan, the Italian football club
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: A singer is performing at an Italian nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: One who intones, chanting or reciting in a singing voice.

clue.text: Look, including books with introduction to hell is Jeremiah's habit

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
incl is the abbreviation for including
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

indicators.note: take the opening letter of hell

explanation.surface: A prophet's habit of looking at Old Testament books with their introduction to hell.
explanation.walkthrough: In Jeremiah 13 the prophet is told to buy and wear a linen loincloth; 'habit' here is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit can be a garment, and the biblical prophet was told to wear a linen waist garment.

clue.text: Prospect having 1000% growth at the start must have hit supply partner

indicators.note: the opening letter as a Roman numeral grows tenfold, five becoming fifty

parts.note: a view is a prospect, an outlook

indicators.note: read as an adverb, supply means in a supple way, bending the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A business prospect with huge early growth must find a supply partner.
explanation.walkthrough: V is Roman five; a tenfold rise gives L, fifty, so VIEW becomes LIEW. 'Must have' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to partner someone in the intimate sense is to sleep with them.

clue.text: Check out six footer's boxing power

indicators.note: enclosing as in a box, so the insect surrounds the letter

parts.note: an insect has six legs, so it is a six-footer
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Take a look at a six-foot boxer's power.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'six footer' sounds like a tall boxer; it is an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, to look something over carefully.

clue.text: Unpaired dance card

parts.note: odd means without a partner, as an odd sock
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' suggests a dance card, but here it is a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an eccentric or amusing person, a slightly peculiar character.

clue.text: Gold — something Trump uses after Tax Officer's support for those speaking publicly

indicators.note: the snooker item comes after the tax officer

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
TO is the abbreviation for tax officer
Judd Trump is a world snooker champion, who plays with a cue

explanation.surface: Gold is what Donald Trump uses after the taxman's backing for his speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trump is not the US president but Judd Trump, the English snooker player.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen showing the script so presenters and politicians can read their words while facing the audience.

clue.text: Group of tongues wagging — ultimately following small party

indicators.note: the language and final letter come after the small letter

parts.note: Hindi names the main language of India and a group of related north Indian languages

indicators.note: takes the last letter of wagging

explanation.surface: Tongues wag at the end of a small party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a lively, noisy celebration or social gathering.

clue.text: Relation coming from International lawn bowling

indicators.note: rolling around, so the letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A relative comes from an international lawn-bowls tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative by marriage, such as a spouse's parent or sibling.

clue.text: Perhaps one Munich let out

indicators.note: out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps from Munich, is let out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is a time, one o'clock, a typical hour for the midday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: One o'clock is a typical example of the midday meal hour.

clue.text: A pedestrian shopping area turning back one that spits

indicators.note: the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a mall is a pedestrianised shopping precinct

explanation.surface: Someone in a shopping precinct turns back to spit.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American animal is notorious for spitting when annoyed.

clue.text: Concede it's not worthwhile scrambling to take in film

indicators.note: the scrambled letters enclose the film
mixing up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone gives up because scrambling to see a film is not worth it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from boxing, where a trainer throws a towel into the ring to admit defeat.
